data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's evidentiary discriminator (comparing the observed joint failure distribution against the same distribution conditioned on operator-level factors) can only be computed after a sufficiently rich failure dataset exists. The problem explicitly asks to identify evidence that would distinguish truly independent failures from failures that merely appear uncorrelated until a shared cause is found. The target's conditioning test presupposes that the shared cause has already manifested in the data, yet it provides no forward-looking evidentiary criterion for distinguishing independence during the critical period when failures merely *appear* uncorrelated and no shared cause has yet been observed. The causal-conditioning mechanism only reveals apparent (not true) independence after the fact; it does not answer what evidence would distinguish the two before the correlated event arrives, leaving the specific evidentiary question the problem poses only partially addressed.
